title: I Just Bought $74,000 in this Crushed AI Stock
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: Joseph Hogue's weekly market update, published 8 November 2026, is a dip-buying tour of 29 AI stocks after a brutal sell-off: the Nasdaq is down over 10% from its peak into correction territory, Nvidia is down 22% in a month and Micron 34%, with Marvell down 50%. He argues the sell-off is overdone because nothing fundamental has changed - hyperscalers plus Oracle are set to spend over $1 trillion on AI in 2027, already locked in and funded - and because a data-center construction slowdown was coming anyway for physical reasons (power generation takes years, high-bandwidth memory is short), so the post-midterm political fears change the messaging, not the demand. He screens five groups - AI infrastructure, memory, AI power, cybersecurity and software - on forward revenue growth and PEG ratio, finding a wide gap between collapsing prices and still-strong fundamentals, AMD being the clearest example (revenue +45%, data-center revenue +97%, yet down a third). His headline action is a real purchase: 700 shares of ServiceNow at $106 each, $74,000, on its orchestration story. He would also pick up Palantir, Micron, SanDisk, Bloom Energy, Fortinet and Zscaler, while holding Palo Alto, CrowdStrike, Okta and Cloudflare as too expensive to add, and pulling back on Arista after its earnings pop. A sponsored Gigastar segment interrupts the analysis. Note: the caption file ends mid-sentence during the Palantir discussion, so the video's closing picks are missing from the captions; 'A net'/'Aenet' is Arista Networks, 'Epic CPUs' is EPYC, and figures like 'Micron revenue growth of 378%' and 'ServiceNow revenue growth of $20 billion' are garbled.

calls.bear_case: He still believes memory is cyclical - 'we're just seeing a super cycle here.'
